newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert sees Q1 EPS at $0.75/shr.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert sees Q1 EPS at $0.75/shr.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co expects to report first-quarter earnings of $0.75 a share when it announces its results next Tuesday, Chief Executive Melvin Goodes told investors on Thursday.
The expected result compares with net earnings of $0.92 a share in the 1996 first quarter, or $0.72 when adjusted for extraordinary items.
"First-quarter sales, excluding exchange, are expected to be virtually unchanged from prior year," the company said.
Goodes told investors at a presentation that the company expected to achieve double-digit sales growth and earnings per share of at least $3.10 for the full year, compared with $2.90 for 1996.
The company said it expected to deliver annual profit growth in the mid-teens for the rest of the century.
Goodes said Warner-Lambert's cholesterol-lowering agent Lipitor and Type II diabetes drug Rezulin should spark a "period of accelerated and sustainable growth."
"We believe that both Lipitor and Rezulin have the potential to be billion-dollar blockbusters," he added.
He said Lipitor has captured an 11.5 percent share of the U.S. market since its launch in late February.

Warner-Lambert said it introduced Rezulin -- the first agent that directly reduces insulin resistance through a unique nuclear mechanism -- in the United States last month. It gave no sales figures on Thursday.
